title: Active Data lets operational registries be edited directly without a governance vote
content:
Two registries in this chunk are marked `[Active Data]` with an accompanying `[Active Data Controller]` document. A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.8.2 specifies the delegate list's controller: Responsible Party is the Operational Facilitator; Trigger is "receipt of onboarding, renewal/re-approval, term-end automatic offboarding, or discretionary offboarding notice from the Spark Foundation"; Update Process is "Direct Edit"; Publication is a notice on the Sky Forum. A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.11.1 does the same for the SRC Membership Registry.

The distinction being drawn is between the **rule** and the **roster**. Changing who may be a Delegate, or what a Delegate must do, is a Root Edit requiring proposal, SRC review and a token holder vote. Recording that a specific delegate lapsed at term end is bookkeeping, and routing it through a vote would be absurd — the outcome is already determined by rules the holders already approved.

Active Data makes that split explicit and constrained. A Direct Edit is not discretionary: it is authorized only by an enumerated trigger, performed by a named party, and must be published. The Facilitator can record a consequence but cannot originate one.

This is what keeps the Atlas usable as a live operational document rather than a snapshot. Contract addresses, delegate rosters, council membership and status flags all change on operational timescales; without a lower-friction lane for them, the Artifact would either be permanently stale or would consume governance capacity on clerical updates. The exposure is that the trigger lists are the only thing distinguishing a permitted Direct Edit from an unauthorized one, and compliance is verified only by whoever reads the forum notice.
description: Delegate and SRC registries are Active Data with a named Responsible Party, defined trigger, Direct Edit process and forum publication — separating bookkeeping from Root Edit amendment.
